title: Teaching young musicians
summary: Howard says he taught many students but none made it big because they wanted to play jazz rather than study.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Did you ever do a lot of teaching?
Did any of your students ever get to be in the big time or make a big name for themselves?
No, they never got to be in the big time. They wouldn't listen to you. They didn't want to play that. Tell you in a minute, listen, you come on and play some jazz with us.
Most of them weren't that serious.
No, they didn't want to study, but I was always trying to learn something.

That was evidently the type of person you have always been. That was at the time say when you had the band, with Lionel Hampton and people like that, some of the big names, were they musicians that were studying or were most of them just sort of natural talent? What am I trying to say here, the type that would be going to school or studying --
Well, some of them and some of them
just wanted to learn the scales, so understand -- what are you doing that for? Ask you a lot of questions.
